main.usage_block:
Lege - Document Processing CLI

Interactive mode: run with no arguments

BASIC USAGE:
    lege <file.pdf> [page-range] [target]
    lege --help
    lege --help env-variables    # show environment variables that influence behavior
    lege --help debug            # show debug/data-generation modes
    lege --status
    lege --licenses
    lege --targets          # list built-in device presets

EXAMPLES:
    lege book.pdf 1-10
    lege book.pdf all 1440x1920
    lege book.pdf 1-5 "Amazon Kindle Scribe (2022)"
    lege book.pdf
    lege (then follow interactive prompts)

TARGET FORMATS:
    - Number (e.g., 1600) keeps proportional width
    - WIDTHxHEIGHT (e.g., 1440x1920)
    - Device name from '--targets' list
    Use 'all' for the page-range when you want every page.

OPTIONS (interactive selection provides these):
    Text formats: jbig2 | ccitt4 | djvu (enter '3' for djvu in interactive)
    Image formats: jpeg | jp2 | none
    Flags: a(layout detection) b(OCR) c(original quality) d(no cover) e(PDF compat) f(force crop) g(invert) h(deskew) i(no binarization) m(center margins) w(crop margins)

ADVANCED (direct CLI, Linux only):
    --language <code>    Use Tesseract OCR language code (e.g., jpn, rus, chi_sim)
                         Requires matching <code>.traineddata in tessdata search paths.

TESTING / DEBUG MODES:
    lege <file.pdf> --pdf-to-png HEIGHT [page-range]
    lege <file.pdf> --crop-areas text|image|both [page-range] [--out DIR] [--format png|jpg] [--deskew]
    lege --png-folder <folder> [--deskew]

Run without arguments for the full interactive guided workflow.

Tip: For environment variables, run: 'lege --help env-variables'.
main.debug_help_block:
Lege - Debug Modes

PDF to PNG (rasterize pages for inspection):
  Usage:   lege <file.pdf> [page_range] --pdf-to-png HEIGHT
  Example: lege book.pdf 1-5 --pdf-to-png 1600

Crop detected layout regions from a PDF into separate images:
  Usage:   lege <file.pdf> [page_range] --crop-areas text|image|both [--out DIR] [--format png|jpg] [--deskew]
  Example: lege book.pdf all --crop-areas image --out ./dataset --format jpg --deskew
  Notes:
    - Regions are numbered per page: page_0001_area_001.jpg, etc.
    - Uses the same layout model as the main pipeline.
    - Output defaults to '<pdf_stem>_areas' next to the input if --out is omitted.

PNG folder inference (images instead of PDF):
  Usage:   lege --png-folder <folder> [--deskew]
  Example: lege --png-folder ./scans --deskew
main.env_variables_help_block:
Lege - Environment Variables

These environment variables influence behavior and discovery paths:

LEGE_ENABLE_PDFIUM_POOL
  Platform:  All (Windows default differs)
  Values:    1|true to enable
  Default:   enabled on non-Windows; disabled on Windows
  Purpose:   Enables a pool of Pdfium instances for parallel rendering in no-layout mode.

LEGE_DATA_DIR
  Platform:  All
  Values:    absolute path
  Default:   unset
  Purpose:   Additional search root for runtime assets (e.g., models, tessdata).

LEGE_ASSET_DIR
  Platform:  All
  Values:    absolute path
  Default:   unset
  Purpose:   Additional search root for runtime assets (e.g., models, tessdata).

LD_LIBRARY_PATH
  Platform:  Linux
  Values:    colon-separated list of paths
  Default:   system default
  Purpose:   On Linux, directories here are also searched for Lege assets (in addition to libraries).

Notes:
- On Windows, Pdfium pooling is disabled by default due to stability concerns; enable via LEGE_ENABLE_PDFIUM_POOL.
- DJVU encoding uses the native Rust encoder path (no external DjVu tools required).
